subject: Human Evolution
title: Cognitive Archaeology
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Cognitive Archaeology.

hook.text: A stone tool is the only thought from a million years ago you can hold in your hand.

buildup.text: Cognitive archaeology reads ancient minds through artifacts: what skills and knowledge each tool implies.

discovery.text: Symmetry, raw material choice, and transport distance each reveal different mental abilities.

twist.text: The absence of tools is informative too—some hominins left no artifacts, suggesting simpler cognition.

climax.text: Every artifact is a frozen decision. Cognitive archaeology decodes the mind behind the hand.

punchline.text: Rocks are the fossils of thought.
